input.task: Build a friendly 2D room planner with a furniture catalog beside a top-down room preview. A select labeled Furniture offers Sofa (EUR600), Chair (EUR120) and Table (EUR240). Start with an empty room and EUR0 total. Add furniture puts the chosen piece into the preview, selects it and updates the price. Give items monotonic integer ids starting at 1; each is a selectable button named Sofa 1, Chair 2, and so on, using its type and id. Show selection clearly. Remove selected deletes that piece and updates the total; disable it when nothing is selected. Label the preview region Room preview. A number input labeled Room width accepts 3 through 8 meters, initially 4. The room depth stays 4 meters, so changing width visibly changes the preview aspect ratio to width / 4. Display the current width and total price in a clear inspector. Keep the plan and inspector usable on a phone. Expose inspection state through window.__planner = { items, width, total }, where each item has id and type, types are Sofa/Chair/Table, width is meters and total is the euro amount. Keep that state current after every action. Use buttons named Add furniture and Remove selected.

input.task: Create a welcoming Three.js interior that looks like a small furnished reading room. Use a 6 by 6 meter floor, two walls, a table, two chairs and a standing lamp. Give the furniture recognizable shapes, pleasing proportions and warm materials, with depth, shadows and a useful initial camera view. Add a Rotate view button that moves the camera around the room while keeping the furnishings in view. A Night mode toggle button starts with aria-pressed=false; toggling it changes aria-pressed and visibly darkens the room while keeping the lamp warm and readable. The canvas must resize with its container on desktop and phone. Expose window.__scene = { scene, camera, renderer } using the actual Three.js objects. For inspection name the scene objects floor, wall-back, wall-left, table, chair-left, chair-right and lamp; furniture may be groups. Name the main room light room-light and make its intensity lower in night mode. Keep the controls outside the canvas so they remain readable and keyboard-operable.

visual_review: Convincing room composition and furniture proportions

input.task: Build a polished, usable Three.js room configurator. Show a 6 by 6 meter floor, two walls, a table, two chairs and a standing lamp, with coherent materials, depth, lighting and shadows. Name their scene objects floor, wall-back, wall-left, table, chair-left, chair-right and lamp, and the main light room-light. Expose the actual Three.js scene, camera and renderer as window.__scene = { scene, camera, renderer, selectedId }; selectedId is the selected furniture object name. Start with the table selected. A select labeled Selected furniture offers Table, Chair left, Chair right and Lamp and updates the scene selection visibly. Number inputs Position X, Position Z and Rotation move the selected object in world meters and rotate it in degrees; a color input labeled Color recolors its main visible material. Keep each furniture center inside the room by clamping X and Z to -2 through 2, and reflect the clamped value in the input. Include a Rotate view camera button and a Night mode toggle with aria-pressed=false initially; night mode lowers room-light intensity and visibly darkens the room while the lamp stays warm. Reset room restores the initial furniture positions, rotations, colors, selection and daytime lighting. Save edits, selection and night mode under localStorage key visual-web-room and restore them after reload, including a reset saved by the user. Keep the canvas and inspector usable on a phone. Respect reduced motion by avoiding automatic decorative camera or furniture animation when that preference is active. Handle interaction and restoration without console errors. Use buttons named Rotate view, Night mode and Reset room.

tier.name: supreme
tier.basis: Untimed estimate, explicitly unvalidated: extend a furnished 3D room into a configurator with selection, world transforms, bounded placement, material editing, reset, saved state and responsive controls. About two hours for interaction/state work and two for scene composition, accessibility and verification. The label needs timed expert confirmation.

visual_review: Room and inspector form a coherent product
Selection and transformations are easy to understand

Phone layout preserves a useful scene and usable controls
